title: CBSE CLASS 6 — English | Active Passive
description: Subject-wise test on Active Passive (English) for CBSE CLASS 6. 50Q.
subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: Choose the correct passive voice form of the sentence: 'She sings a beautiful song.'

options.text: A beautiful song is sung by her.
options.explanation: Correct passive form for simple present tense.

options.text: A beautiful song was sung by her.
options.explanation: Incorrect tense; 'was' is used for simple past.

options.text: A beautiful song will be sung by her.
options.explanation: Incorrect tense; 'will be' is used for simple future.

options.text: A beautiful song is sang by her.
options.explanation: Incorrect verb form; 'sang' is V2, not V3.

questions.explanation: In simple present active voice (Subject + V1/V5 + Object), the passive voice structure is (Object + is/am/are + V3 + by + Subject). 'Sings' is V5, so 'is sung' is the correct passive form.
questions.hint: Identify the correct form of 'to be' and past participle for the given sentence.
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: Identify the sentence that is in the passive voice.

options.text: The children play in the park.
options.explanation: Active voice sentence with no 'to be' verb.

options.text: My mother bakes a cake every Sunday.
options.explanation: Active voice sentence with no 'to be' verb.

options.text: The letter was written by him.
options.explanation: Passive voice sentence with 'was' + past participle + 'by'.

options.text: Birds build nests.
options.explanation: Active voice sentence with no 'to be' verb.

questions.explanation: A passive voice sentence typically uses a form of 'to be' (was) followed by the past participle (written) and often includes 'by' followed by the doer of the action.
questions.hint: Look for the structure: Object + form of 'to be' + past participle + (by + doer).
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct passive form: 'The delicious cookies ______ by my grandmother.'

options.text: is baked
options.explanation: Incorrect; 'is' is used for singular subjects.

options.text: are baked
options.explanation: Correct; 'are' matches the plural subject 'cookies'.

options.text: was baked
options.explanation: Incorrect; 'was' is used for singular subjects in past tense.

options.text: will bake
options.explanation: Incorrect; 'will bake' is active voice and future tense.

questions.explanation: 'Cookies' is a plural noun, so it requires 'are'. The action is completed, suggesting a simple present passive or past passive. Given the options, 'are baked' fits the general context of someone regularly making cookies.
questions.hint: Consider the number of the subject and the correct form of 'to be' for passive voice.
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: Convert the following sentence into passive voice: 'He broke the window.'

options.text: The window is broken by him.
options.explanation: Incorrect tense; 'is' is used for simple present.

options.text: The window was broken by him.
options.explanation: Correct; 'was' matches the past tense of the active sentence.

options.text: The window will be broken by him.
options.explanation: Incorrect tense; 'will be' is used for simple future.

options.text: The window has been broken by him.
options.explanation: Incorrect tense; 'has been' is used for present perfect.

questions.explanation: The active sentence 'He broke the window' is in the simple past tense (Subject + V2 + Object). The passive voice for simple past is (Object + was/were + V3 + by + Subject).
questions.hint: Identify the correct form of 'to be' (was/were) and the past participle of the verb.
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: Choose the correct passive voice sentence for: 'They will build a new school.'

options.text: A new school is built by them.
options.explanation: Incorrect tense; 'is' is used for simple present.

options.text: A new school was built by them.
options.explanation: Incorrect tense; 'was' is used for simple past.

options.text: A new school will be built by them.
options.explanation: Correct; 'will be' matches the future tense of the active sentence.

options.text: A new school has been built by them.
options.explanation: Incorrect tense; 'has been' is used for present perfect.

questions.explanation: The active sentence is in the simple future tense (Subject + will + V1 + Object). The passive voice for simple future is (Object + will be + V3 + by + Subject).
questions.hint: Identify the correct structure for passive voice in simple future tense.
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: Which of the following sentences correctly converts 'The gardener is watering the plants' into passive voice?

options.text: The plants are watered by the gardener.
options.explanation: Incorrect; 'are watered' is simple present passive, not continuous.

options.text: The plants were being watered by the gardener.
options.explanation: Incorrect; 'were being' is past continuous passive.

options.text: The plants are being watered by the gardener.
options.explanation: Correct; 'are being' matches the present continuous tense.

options.text: The plants will be watered by the gardener.
options.explanation: Incorrect; 'will be' is simple future passive.

questions.explanation: The active sentence is in the present continuous tense (Subject + is/am/are + V-ing + Object). The passive voice for present continuous is (Object + is/am/are + being + V3 + by + Subject).
questions.hint: Identify the correct form of 'to be' and the addition of 'being' for present continuous passive voice.
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: Convert the imperative sentence 'Open the door.' into passive voice.

options.text: The door is opened.
options.explanation: Incorrect; does not follow the imperative passive structure.

options.text: Let the door be opened.
options.explanation: Correct; follows the imperative passive structure.

options.text: The door should be opened.
options.explanation: Incorrect; uses 'should' instead of 'Let'.

options.text: You are requested to open the door.
options.explanation: Incorrect; this is a polite request, not passive voice.

questions.explanation: For imperative sentences (commands), the passive voice typically uses the structure 'Let + Object + be + V3'.
questions.hint: Imperative sentences in passive voice often start with 'Let' followed by the object and 'be' + past participle.
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: Which sentence uses the passive voice to emphasize the action rather than the doer?

options.text: My brother painted this picture.
options.explanation: Active voice; emphasizes the doer ('my brother').

options.text: The picture was painted by my brother.
options.explanation: Passive voice; emphasizes the action ('was painted') and the object ('the picture').

options.text: They are painting a mural.
options.explanation: Active voice; emphasizes the doer ('they').

options.text: The artist painted a beautiful portrait.
options.explanation: Active voice; emphasizes the doer ('the artist').

questions.explanation: Passive voice is often used when the action or the object receiving the action is more important than the doer. Here, 'the picture' and the action 'was painted' are emphasized.
questions.hint: Look for a sentence where the object of the action is the subject, and the doer is mentioned with 'by'.
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question:
**Assertion (A):** The sentence 'The ball was hit by the batsman.' is in the passive voice.
**Reason (R):** In passive voice, the object of the active sentence becomes the subject, and a form of 'be' verb is used with the past participle.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: The reason is the correct explanation for the assertion.

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
options.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are true.

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
options.explanation: The assertion is true.

questions.explanation: The assertion is true because 'The ball was hit by the batsman' follows the passive structure (Object + was/were + V3 + by + Subject). The reason correctly defines the key characteristics of passive voice, explaining why the assertion is true.
questions.hint: Evaluate both the assertion and the reason separately and determine if the reason correctly explains the assertion.
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question:
Read the following passage:
'Yesterday, our school held its annual sports day. Many events were organized. Rahul won the 100-meter race. Later, prizes were distributed to the winners by the principal. Everyone enjoyed the day.'
Which sentence from the passage, if converted to active voice, would be: 'The principal distributed prizes to the winners.'?

options.text: Many events were organized.
options.explanation: Does not match the given active voice sentence.

options.text: Rahul won the 100-meter race.
options.explanation: Does not match the given active voice sentence.

options.text: Later, prizes were distributed to the winners by the principal.
options.explanation: This passive voice sentence converts to the given active voice sentence.

options.text: Everyone enjoyed the day.
options.explanation: Does not match the given active voice sentence.

questions.explanation: The sentence 'Later, prizes were distributed to the winners by the principal' is in passive voice (Prizes = object, were distributed = V3, by the principal = doer). Converting this to active voice means making 'the principal' the subject, leading to 'The principal distributed prizes to the winners.'
questions.hint: Identify the passive voice sentence in the passage and convert it to active voice to match the given sentence.
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: Choose the correct passive voice for the sentence: 'The gardener waters the plants.'

options.text: The plants are watered by the gardener.
options.explanation: Correct passive voice for the given sentence.

options.text: The plants were watered by the gardener.
options.explanation: Incorrect tense; 'were' is used for past tense, but the original sentence is in present tense.

options.text: The plants water the gardener.
options.explanation: This reverses the subject and object, making it an active voice sentence.

options.text: The gardener is watered by the plants.
options.explanation: This reverses the action and is grammatically incorrect for the given sentence.

questions.explanation: In the active voice, 'the gardener' is the subject and 'the plants' is the object. In simple present tense, the passive voice uses 'is/are' + past participle. So, 'The plants' (plural) takes 'are' and the past participle of 'water' is 'watered'.
questions.hint: Identify the subject and object in the active sentence and convert it to passive voice using 'are' + past participle.
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: Identify the sentence that is in the passive voice.

options.text: The children play games.
options.explanation: This is an active voice sentence where the subject 'children' performs the action.

options.text: My mother bakes a cake.
options.explanation: This is an active voice sentence where the subject 'mother' performs the action.

options.text: A beautiful song was sung by her.
options.explanation: This sentence is in passive voice with 'was' + past participle 'sung' + 'by' + agent 'her'.

options.text: He reads a newspaper every morning.
options.explanation: This is an active voice sentence where the subject 'he' performs the action.

questions.explanation: This sentence has the structure 'be' (was) + past participle (sung) + 'by' + agent (her), which is characteristic of the passive voice. The other sentences have the subject performing the action directly.
questions.hint: Look for the structure 'be' verb + past participle + 'by' + agent.
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: Convert the following sentence into passive voice: 'She wrote a letter yesterday.'

options.text: A letter is written by her yesterday.
options.explanation: Incorrect tense; 'is' is used for present tense, but the original sentence is in past tense.

options.text: A letter was written by her yesterday.
options.explanation: Correct passive voice for the given sentence.

options.text: She was written a letter yesterday.
options.explanation: Incorrect structure; the object 'a letter' should be the subject in passive voice.

options.text: Yesterday, she was writing a letter.
options.explanation: This is in past continuous tense, not passive voice.

questions.explanation: The active sentence is in the simple past tense. For simple past passive, we use 'was/were' + past participle. 'A letter' (singular) takes 'was', and the past participle of 'write' is 'written'.
questions.hint: Change the tense to past passive and ensure the subject and object are correctly placed.
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct passive form: 'The lost dog _______ by a kind lady.'

options.text: found
options.explanation: Incorrect; this is the simple past tense, not passive voice.

options.text: was found
options.explanation: Correct passive voice in simple past tense.

options.text: finds
options.explanation: Incorrect tense; 'finds' is present tense.

options.text: is finding
options.explanation: Incorrect tense; 'is finding' is present continuous tense.

questions.explanation: The sentence indicates an action completed in the past where the dog is the receiver of the action (passive). 'Was found' correctly forms the simple past passive voice.
questions.hint: Identify the tense and use 'was/were' + past participle.

questions.question: Choose the correct passive voice for the sentence: 'I will finish the homework.'

options.text: The homework will be finished by me.
options.explanation: Correct passive voice for the given sentence.

options.text: The homework is finished by me.
options.explanation: Incorrect tense; 'is' is used for present tense, but the original sentence is in future tense.

options.explanation: Incorrect tense; 'was' is used for past tense, but the original sentence is in future tense.

options.text: I will be finished by the homework.
options.explanation: Incorrect structure; the object 'homework' should be the subject in passive voice.

questions.question: Convert the following sentence into passive voice: 'He did not break the glass.'

options.text: The glass was not broken by him.
options.explanation: Correct passive voice for the given sentence.

options.text: The glass is not broken by him.
options.explanation: Incorrect tense; 'is' is used for present tense, but the original sentence is in past tense.

options.explanation: Incorrect structure; the object 'glass' should be the subject in passive voice.

options.text: The glass did not break by him.
options.explanation: Incorrect structure; 'did not break' is active voice.

questions.explanation: The active sentence is in the simple past negative tense. In passive voice, the object 'the glass' becomes the subject, and the structure becomes 'was not' + past participle ('broken') + 'by him'.
questions.hint: Convert the negative past tense sentence to passive voice using 'was not' + past participle.
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct passive transformation of 'My mother cooks delicious food'?

options.text: Delicious food is cooked by my mother.
options.explanation: Correct passive voice for the given sentence.

options.text: Delicious food was cooked by my mother.
options.explanation: Incorrect tense; 'was' is used for past tense, but the original sentence is in present tense.

options.text: My mother is cooked by delicious food.
options.explanation: Incorrect structure; the object 'food' should be the subject in passive voice.

options.text: Delicious food cooks my mother.
options.explanation: Incorrect structure; this reverses the subject and object.

questions.explanation: The active sentence is in the simple present tense. The passive form requires 'is/are' + past participle. 'Delicious food' (singular, referring to the entire meal) takes 'is', and 'cooks' becomes 'cooked'.

questions.question: Complete the sentence with the appropriate passive form: 'Many trees _______ by the storm last night.'

options.text: fell
options.explanation: Incorrect; 'fell' is the simple past tense, not passive voice.

options.text: were fallen
options.explanation: Incorrect; 'fallen' is the past participle of 'fall', not 'fell'.

options.text: were felled
options.explanation: Correct passive voice using the past participle 'felled'.

options.text: are falling
options.explanation: Incorrect tense; 'are falling' is present continuous tense.

questions.explanation: The verb 'felled' (past participle of 'fell' meaning to cut down a tree) is used when trees are brought down by an external force, like a storm. The action happened last night (past), and the trees are the recipients of the action (passive), so 'were felled' is correct. 'Fallen' is the past participle of 'fall' (to drop down naturally).
questions.hint: Identify the correct past participle for the verb 'fell' in the context of trees being cut down.
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: **Assertion (A):** The sentence 'The cat chased the mouse' is in the active voice. **Reason (R):** In the active voice, the subject performs the action described by the verb.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: The reason is the correct explanation for the assertion.

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
options.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are true.

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
options.explanation: The assertion is true.

questions.explanation: The assertion is true because 'the cat' (subject) is performing the action 'chased'. The reason is also true and directly explains why the sentence is in the active voice.
questions.hint: Understand the definition of active voice and apply it to the given sentence.
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: Read the following sentence: 'People speak English all over the world.' If you want to change this sentence into the passive voice, which option correctly represents the passive form?

options.text: English is spoken by people all over the world.
options.explanation: Correct passive voice for the given sentence.

options.text: English was spoken by people all over the world.
options.explanation: Incorrect tense; 'was' is used for past tense, but the original sentence is in present tense.

options.text: English speaks people all over the world.
options.explanation: Incorrect structure; this reverses the subject and object.

options.text: People are spoken English all over the world.
options.explanation: Incorrect structure; 'are spoken' is not the correct passive form for this sentence.

questions.explanation: The original sentence is in the simple present tense. To convert it to passive voice, the object 'English' becomes the subject, followed by 'is' (for simple present singular subject) and the past participle of 'speak' (spoken). The phrase 'by people' can be included, and 'all over the world' remains.
questions.hint: Convert the simple present tense sentence to passive voice by making 'English' the subject and using 'is' + past participle.
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct passive voice sentence for 'The gardener waters the plants every morning.'?

questions.hint: Identify the tense and subject-verb agreement in the active sentence.

questions.question: Convert the sentence 'The children are drawing beautiful pictures.' into passive voice.

options.text: Beautiful pictures are being drawn by the children.
options.explanation: Correct passive form for present continuous tense with plural subject.

options.text: Beautiful pictures is being drawn by the children.
options.explanation: Uses 'is' which is incorrect for plural subject.

questions.question: **Assertion (A):** The sentence 'The ball was hit by the player' is in passive voice. **Reason (R):** In the passive voice, the subject performs the action. Choose the correct option.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Assertion is true, but Reason is false and does not explain the assertion.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Reason is false, so this option is invalid.

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
options.explanation: Assertion is true, but Reason is false as the subject in passive voice receives the action.

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
options.explanation: Assertion is true, so this option is invalid.

questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is true because 'was hit' is the passive form. However, Reason (R) is false because in the passive voice, the subject *receives* the action, it does not perform it. The doer of the action (the player) is usually mentioned with 'by'.
questions.hint: Understand the definition of passive voice and the role of the subject.
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: Convert the sentence 'People eat rice in many countries.' into passive voice.

options.text: Rice is eaten by people in many countries.
options.explanation: Grammatically correct but less natural as the doer 'people' is included unnecessarily.

options.text: Rice is eaten in many countries.
options.explanation: Correct and natural passive form where the doer is omitted for conciseness.

options.text: Rice was eaten in many countries.
options.explanation: Uses past tense 'was' which is incorrect for the given active sentence.

options.text: Rice will be eaten by people in many countries.
options.explanation: Uses future tense 'will be' which is incorrect for the given active sentence.

questions.explanation: When the doer of the action (the agent), like 'people', is general or unimportant, it is often omitted in the passive voice for conciseness and natural flow. While option A is grammatically correct, option B is the more commonly preferred and natural passive form in such cases.
questions.hint: Consider whether the doer of the action needs to be mentioned in the passive voice.
questions.subject: cbse6-english

options.explanation: This is in passive voice as the subject ('the letter') receives the action.

questions.explanation: The active voice is when the subject performs the action. Here, 'The teacher' is the subject performing the action of praising.
questions.hint: Active voice sentences have the subject performing the action directly.

questions.question: Identify the passive form of the sentence: 'The chef cooks the food.'

options.text: The food is cooked by the chef.
options.explanation: This is the correct passive form of the given sentence.
